message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze this OIML certificate carefully.

Certificate details:
- Number: R117/2007-A-NL1-22.05 revision 3
- Scheme: A
- Project number: 3774992
- Page total: 4
- Member State: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 6 March 2024
- OIML issuer: NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1 → oiml_issuer_id: "NL1"

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V.
- Address: Thijsseweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, the Netherlands
- Person responsible: M.Ph.D. Schmidt
- Phone: +31 88 636 2332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- oiml_issuer_id: NL1

Applicants:
- Micro Motion, Inc., 7070 Winchester Circle, Boulder, Colorado 80301, United States of America
(Also the manufacturer — "Applicant and Manufacturer")

Manufacturers:
- Same as applicant: Micro Motion, Inc.

Certified type:
- Category: "Measuring system" — actually it's a "measuring device (ultrasonic sensor with belonging electronics)" — R117-1 is "Dynamic measuring systems for liquids other than water". Category could be "Measuring system" or "Ultrasonic flowmeter". The certificate says "A measuring device (ultrasonic sensor with belonging electronics)". I'll use "Measuring system" as category, and description "ultrasonic sensor with belonging electronics". Actually let me think — R117-1: 2007 "Dynamic measuring systems for liquids other than water". The certified type is a measuring device — an ultrasonic sensor with belonging electronics. Category options in schema: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ... So "Measuring system" fits best. Or "Ultrasonic flow meter". I'll go with "Measuring system".

- type_designations: "Model 3814", "Model 3818" (Manufacturer's mark: Rosemount). So type_designations: ["Model 3814", "Model 3818"]. Maybe include "3814" and "3818". I'll use ["Model 3814", "Model 3818"] or ["3814", "3818"]. Let me use ["Model 3814", "Model 3818"].

- module_designation: null or "Not applicable"? The cert doesn't mention modules. Omit or null. I'll set to null. Actually rule 8: don't fabricate; omit if not present. But schema shows module_designation field. I'll set null.

- description: "Ultrasonic sensor with belonging electronics" — manufacturer's mark Rosemount.

Model family: The cert covers a family of instruments (Table 2 "General characteristics of the family of instruments"). Meter sizes: 4", 6", 8", 10", 12", 16", 18". But also there are two type designations 3814 and 3818. Hmm. The family is defined by meter size. Table 3 gives transducers per meter size range (4"-10" vs 12"-18") with LT-01..LT-09 variants differing by liquid temperature and viscosity range.

Model family:
- family_name: null (no explicit family name; "family of instruments" mentioned). Could say null.
- models: one entry per meter size:
  - {"model_id": "4\"", "label": "Meter size 4 inch", attributes: {...}}
  - Actually the schema: models[]: {model_id, label, attributes{}}. Attributes optional.

Should model_id be the meter size or combine type + size? The types are 3814 and 3818; the family table is by meter size. The transducer table maps meter size ranges to LT-xx transducers. I'll use model_id as meter size: "4\"", "6\"", etc. Hmm, but what distinguishes 3814 vs 3818? Not clear from markdown. Possibly 3814 is for 4"-10" and 3818 for 12"-18"? Not stated. Don't fabricate.

I'll create models for each meter size: 4", 6", 8", 10", 12", 16", 18".

Components: The certified type is "ultrasonic sensor with belonging electronics". Transducers LT-01 through LT-09 are named sub-assemblies. So components[] could include:
- role: "transducer", type_designations: ["LT-01", "LT-02"...]. Wait, the transducer table: 4"-10" sizes column: LT-01, LT-04, LT-06, LT-08; 12"-18" column: LT-03, LT-05, LT-07, LT-09. Each row pairs a transducer for 4"-10" with one for 12"-18", with same liquid temperature range and viscosity.

Row 1: LT-01 (4"-10"), LT-03 (12"-18"), -50°C to 100°C, up to 130 cst
Row 2: LT-04, LT-05, -50°C to 150°C, up to 1000 cst
Row 3: LT-06, LT-07, -200°C to 60°C, up to 130 cst
Row 4: LT-08, LT-09, -50°C to 150°C, up to 130 cst

So transducers are per-variant. How to represent? Options:
1. components[] entries for each transducer with characteristics (temperature range, viscosity).
2. config_level entries: attribute "liquid_temperature_range" with axis "transducer / meter size".

The transducer choice depends on the meter size and desired temperature/viscosity range. This is like a configuration axis.

I think the best representation:
- matrix_tables[] for Table 3 with name "General characteristics of the transducers", columns: ["transducer_4_to_10_inch", "transducer_12_to_18_inch", "liquid_temperature_range", "viscosity_range"], rows for the 4 rows.
- components[]: maybe one entry role "ultrasonic transducer" with type_designations LT-01, LT-03, LT-04, LT-05, LT-06, LT-07, LT-08, LT-09, alternatives? They're alternatives depending on configuration. Hmm.

The rule 6: For complex instruments record each as components[] entry with role, type_designations, sub-characteristics. When cert offers alternatives record alternatives: "OR".

I could do components entries:
- {role: "measuring sensor", type_designations: ["Model 3814", "Model 3818"]} — hmm, actually the whole certified type is the ultrasonic sensor with electronics.

Actually the certified type itself is the "ultrasonic sensor with belonging electronics" — the transducers LT-xx are part of it. Let me include components:
- {role: "ultrasonic transducer", type_designations: ["LT-01", "LT-03", "LT-04", "LT-05", "LT-06", "LT-07", "LT-08", "LT-09"], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {...}} — but each transducer has different temp range.

Better: use config_level for temperature/viscosity:
config_level[]:
- attribute: "liquid_temperature_range", axis: "transducer variant and meter size range", values: [{condition: "LT-01 (4\"-10\") / LT-03 (12\"-18\")", value: {min:-50,max:100}, unit_symbol: "°C"}, ...]

That seems reasonable per rule 5.

Also components could be:
- {role: "transducer", type_designations: ["LT-01", "LT-04", "LT-06", "LT-08"], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {"applicable_meter_sizes": "4\"-10\""}}
- {role: "transducer", type_designations: ["LT-03", "LT-05", "LT-07", "LT-09"], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {"applicable_meter_sizes": "12\"-18\""}}

Hmm, that's a bit arbitrary. Alternatively one component entry listing all with role "ultrasonic transducer". And use config_level for the temperature/viscosity mapping. I'll do:

components[]:
1. {role: "ultrasonic transducer", type_designations: ["LT-01","LT-03","LT-04","LT-05","LT-06","LT-07","LT-08","LT-09"], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {}} — plus maybe "selection_by_meter_size" characteristics.

Actually, let me reconsider. The transducer selection is tied to meter size ranges and temperature/viscosity rating. Each LT-xx has specific characteristics:

LT-01: 4"-10", -50 to 100 °C, ≤130 cst
LT-04: 4"-10", -50 to 150 °C, ≤1000 cst
LT-06: 4"-10", -200 to 60 °C, ≤130 cst
LT-08: 4"-10", -50 to 150 °C, ≤130 cst
LT-03: 12"-18", -50 to 100 °C, ≤130 cst
LT-05: 12"-18", -50 to 150 °C, ≤1000 cst
LT-07: 12"-18", -200 to 60 °C, ≤130 cst
LT-09: 12"-18", -50 to 150 °C, ≤130 cst

I could model each transducer as its own component entry with characteristics:
components: [
  {role: "ultrasonic transducer", type_designations: ["LT-01"], characteristics: {applicable_meter_sizes: "4\"–10\"", liquid_temperature_range: {...}, viscosity_range: {...}}},
  ...
]

That's 8 entries — verbose but precise. Alternatively group. I think listing each is more faithful. But maybe too verbose; the matrix_tables preserves Table 3 anyway. Let me do both: components with each transducer and its characteristics, plus matrix_tables for Table 3, plus config_level entries for temperature range per transducer.

Hmm, the schema says components[] include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies. The cert names transducers LT-01..LT-09. So include them.

Let me decide: components[] with 8 entries, each with role "ultrasonic transducer", type_designations [LT-xx], characteristics including applicable meter sizes, liquid temperature range, viscosity range.

Actually, to keep it manageable, maybe two component entries grouped by meter size range with alternatives "OR"? But then temperature/viscosity characteristics differ per transducer within the group. I'll go with 8 individual entries — precise.

Characteristics type_level (Table 1):
- number_of_sound_paths: 4, unit null
- sound_frequency: 1.0, unit "MHz" (convert 1,0 → 1.0)
- path_angle: 60, unit "°" — unit_symbol "°" or "degree"? The rule says match canonical Unicode form; "°" is fine. Maybe "°". I'll use "°". Hmm, but the example in the instructions uses "°C" for temperature. For angle, "°" alone. unit_id maybe "u:degree". I'll leave unit_id null to be safe. Actually I could put "u:degree" — I'm not 100% sure of unitsdb ID. Leave null.
- maximum_pressure: 300, unit "bar(g)" — value 300, unit_symbol "bar(g)"? Units: "bar" with gauge note. I'll use unit_symbol "bar" and maybe value 300... but "(g)" indicates gauge pressure. Could record unit_symbol as "bar(g)" raw. Hmm. The rule: unit_symbol should be a raw symbol; unitsdb lookup by caller. "bar(g)" isn't standard; I'll use "bar" and add note? There's no note field except footnote_markers. I could keep unit_symbol "bar(g)" as raw symbol since it's what the cert says. I think "bar(g)" is acceptable as raw. Hmm, but caller looks up unit_symbol in unitsdb; "bar(g)" won't match. Better: unit_symbol "bar", and value 300, and maybe add a separate note? There's no notes field. I'll just use "bar(g)"? Let me think about what's more useful. The schema has footnote_markers for value. I could put the gauge indicator in unit_symbol raw "bar(g)". I'll go with "bar(g)" since it preserves information, and unit_id null. Actually, let me reconsider: rule 3 examples show raw symbols like "%vol" not in unitsdb, using raw symbol. So "bar(g)" as raw symbol is consistent.
- environmental_class: "M2" and electromagnetic class "E2"? Environmental classes "M2 / E2". I'd record as two characteristics: environmental_class_m: "M2"? Hmm. OIML: M = mechanical environment class, E = climatic? Actually for R117: environmental classes M2/E2. I'll record:
  - "environmental_class": {value: "M2 / E2"}? Or split: mechanical_environment_class: "M2", climatic_environment_class: "E2". Splitting is cleaner. But is E2 climatic? In WELMEC/OIML D 11: E = climatic environment classes, M = mechanical environment classes. Yes. But don't over-interpret; I'll record environmental_class: "M2 / E2" as a single string value? Hmm, structured value shape: {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. value can be string "M2 / E2". That's fine. Alternatively split into two entries: mechanical_environment_class "M2", climatic_environment_class "E2". I'll do the split as it's more useful, and note canonical labels. Actually to be safe I'll do a single "environmental_class" with value "M2 / E2". Hmm. The instruction says canonical labels, structured values. I'll split: "mechanical_environment_class": "M2", "climatic_environment_class": "E2"? That's interpretation. M2/E2 — in OIML D11, classes for mechanical environment M1-M3 and climatic... actually E is "electromagnetic environment"? Let me recall: OIML D 11 "General requirements for measuring instruments – Environmental conditions": climatic environment classes (1-4H?), mechanical environment classes M1-M3, electromagnetic environment classes E1-E5? Hmm, actually in OIML D11:2013, there are: climatic (C?), mechanical (M), electromagnetic (E). I believe E = electromagnetic environment class, M = mechanical environment class. For example, in MID/OIML: "E2, M2" — E2 electromagnetic, M2 mechanical. Yes: MID Annex I: climatic environment rating... In WELMEC 2.4? For NAWI (R76), "environmental class" per D11: E = electromagnetic? Let me just record as single value "M2 / E2" under "environmental_class". That avoids misinterpretation. I'll do that.
- ambient_temperature_range: {min: -40, max: 55}, unit "°C"
- product_temperature_range: "See table 3" — that's a reference, not a value. Could record as model/config level. I'll skip type_level and note it's per transducer config (covered in Table 3). Or record value "See table 3" — not a value really. I'll handle via config_level with liquid/product temperature per transducer. Skip in type_level.
- minimum_maximum_flow_rate: "See table 2; Bi-directional (if calibration performed in both flow directions)" — covered by model_level qmin/qmax. Also record "flow_direction": "Bi-directional (if calibration performed in both flow directions)" as type_level string. I'll add "flow_direction": {value: "bi-directional"}? The text: "Bi-directional (if calibration performed in both flow directions)". I'll record value as string "Bi-directional (if calibration performed in both flow directions)". Hmm, keep as is.
- power_supply_voltage: 10.4 … 36 V DC → value {min: 10.4, max: 36}, unit "V". Also power_supply_type: "DC".
- minimum_measured_quantity: per meter size — model_level: 1, 2, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 m³.
- software_identification: "See table 4" — skip or capture in matrix_tables (Table 4).

Table 2 → model_level characteristics:

- maximum_flow_rate: 360, 720, 1450, 2250, 3170, 4890, 6334 m³/h
- minimum_reynolds_number: 10000, 10000, 6000, 6000, 6000, 10000, 10000 (unit "-" dimensionless)
